title: Built a browser-based MiG-21 flying/recon experience with Three.js + AI
author: 2600th
selftext:
I recently watched *Operation Safed Sagar* on Netflix and it gave me the idea to experiment with recreating the feeling of a high-altitude reconnaissance mission as an interactive browser experience.

So I built one.

You fly a MiG-21 across a snowy mountainous landscape, navigate through the terrain and photograph enemy positions for reconnaissance.

A large part of the development was AI-assisted, including iterations on gameplay, flight feel, camera, procedural environment, effects and overall polish.

It’s more of an interactive experiment than a historically accurate simulator, but I had a lot of fun seeing how far a browser + Three.js + current AI coding tools could be pushed.

Would especially love feedback on the **flight controls, camera feel, terrain and performance**.

Play: [https://oss-web-3d.vercel.app/](https://oss-web-3d.vercel.app/)

Source: [https://github.com/2600th/oss-web-3d](https://github.com/2600th/oss-web-3d)

comments.author: impact_ftw
comments.body:
Flight Controls need work. Options are ignored entirely and for anything browser based you need to avoid using ctrl.

also speed does not feel right. unless you boost everywhere, youll loose speed and stall.

replies.author: 2600th
replies.body: Thanks! Have replaced Ctrl with X to avoid browser conflicts and adjusted Assisted flight so sustained turns no longer require constant boost to prevent stalling.
